clue.text: Prince needing good fortune and courage

parts.note: good fortune is luck

explanation.surface: A fairytale prince who needs both a lucky break and bravery to win the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having nerve or bravery in the face of danger is showing spirit, or pluck.

clue.text: Something querying the abbot's aim?

parts.note: an abbot heads a religious order, so his aim or purpose is the point of his order; the phrase is also a procedural query raised in a meeting

explanation.surface: A monk wondering aloud what the head of the monastery is trying to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: In a formal meeting, a member who questions whether the rules are being followed raises this; read literally it is the purpose of a monastic community.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a procedural objection in a debate questions the conduct of business, and here also the purpose of a monastic community.

clue.text: Deliverymen bringing ales round, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of the words ales round might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Draymen delivering beer kegs by taking them round the pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who take goods off a lorry at the destination are the people doing the delivery, so deliverymen fits.

clue.text: Amount of knowledge always on the rise in African country

parts.note: ken is range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the rise means the word for always is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Literacy and learning are steadily improving in an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an East African nation whose capital is Nairobi.

clue.text: Substantial part reduced by end of day and cut back by start of year

indicators.note: reduced means the word for part loses its final letter

parts.note: a part in a play is a role

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word day
back means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to cut is to lop

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the word year

explanation.surface: A large share is cut down by the day's close and trimmed again as the new year begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' does double duty here as synonym and reversal signal: LOP reversed gives POL.
explanation.definitionFit: Substantial in the jocular sense of plump or chubby, a word for a rotund person.

clue.text: Deliveryman, perhaps, making a fist of it?

definitions.text: Deliveryman, perhaps, making a fist of it?

parts.words: Deliveryman, perhaps, making a fist of it?
parts.note: fist is slang for handwriting, so making a fist of it is writing; a round, clear style of penmanship is the answer, and a cricket bowler (a deliveryman) bowls with his hand round

explanation.surface: A delivery driver making a poor job of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fist' is old slang for handwriting, and 'deliveryman' hints at a bowler in cricket, who delivers the ball by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a bold, rounded style of penmanship, with fist meaning a person's handwriting.

clue.text: No good in access to computer getting cut

indicators.note: No here says the abbreviation for good is absent from the word for computer access

parts.note: to log in is to gain access to a computer

explanation.surface: Without decent computer access, someone finds their connection cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a verb for being disconnected; it is the butcher's noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a joint of meat from the back of the animal is a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Forerunner's power returns with support of soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, the support of something sits under it, so the soldiers come last

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
something that recurs returns again
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A predecessor's strength comes back once the troops are behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a predecessor or harbinger that comes before and paves the way.

clue.text: Reverse of determination not half shown by this failure

indicators.note: Reverse of means the shortened word is read backwards
not half keeps only the first half of the word for determination

parts.note: resolution is firm determination

explanation.surface: A failure is someone who shows the opposite of resolve, and not even half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves RESOL, which 'Reverse of' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who fails or is beaten, a no-hoper.

clue.text: Group of stars unravels inside, becoming dysfunctional

indicators.note: something becoming dysfunctional is breaking down, so the letters of unravels inside fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Something comes apart internally and stops working properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Old astronomical term for a galaxy, a vast group of stars beyond our own Milky Way.

clue.text: Head of Union drained employee, initially blocking stevedore's transport

indicators.note: blocking means these letters sit inside the word for stevedore, stopping it up

parts.note: a stevedore loads and unloads ships, a docker

indicators.note: Head of takes the first letter of the word Union

parts.note: something drained has been bled

indicators.note: initially keeps only the opening letter of the word employee, dropping all the rest

explanation.surface: A union leader worn out by an employee's dispute at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is a vague definition for a two-storey bus; the surface's union and employee belong to industrial relations, not buses.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bus with two levels is a form of public transport.

clue.text: Most of players will need support of course, and supply of drink

indicators.note: Most of drops the last letter of the word for players

parts.note: a team is a group of players
a caddy supports a golfer on the course by carrying clubs

explanation.surface: Golfers on the course need a caddie and something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small tin or box holds a household supply of the leaves for making a hot drink.

clue.text: Book band having no status but retaining skill

indicators.note: retaining means the letters for skill are held inside the shortened band name
having no says the word status is dropped from the band's name

parts.note: Status Quo is a British rock band
the clue word status is removed as written
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A band without any standing that still keeps its talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo is a long-running British rock band; drop 'Status' and QUO remains to hold ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a book size made from sheets folded twice into four leaves, so a book.

clue.text: Dampness in the air to get on part of instrument

parts.note: a fret, or sea fret, is a coastal mist
to board a train or bus is to get on it

explanation.surface: Humidity making it hard to play a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea fret is a mist rolling in off the North Sea, a term used on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ridged strip on a guitar neck where fingers press the strings.

clue.text: Working with a role in live French costume drama may involve me

definitions.text: French costume drama may involve me

indicators.note: in means the working-with-a-role letters sit inside the word for live

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a machine that is on is working
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: An actor with a role in a live French period drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French emperor Napoleon's surname, a figure who might appear in a French period drama.

clue.text: Sort of acted upset over daughter being engaged by a shady group

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second
in a down clue upset means the word for acted is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to mime is to act without words, a sort of acting

indicators.note: being engaged by means the daughter is held inside the word for a

parts.note: a can mean one

explanation.surface: A daughter who acted out her upset over being engaged to a dubious man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests betrothal but means held inside; 'a' supplies ONE, as in 'a hundred' for one hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a class of disreputable people on the fringes of respectable society.

clue.text: Rough country area that is an uneven place

parts.note: sc., short for scilicet, means namely or that is
in bowls, a rub is an unevenness in the ground

explanation.surface: A rugged rural spot described as bumpy terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game of bowls, a rub is an unevenness of the green that deflects the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: land covered in stunted trees and bushes, rough country.

clue.text: Becoming aware of powder blowing top in revolution

indicators.note: in places the shortened powder inside the word for revolution

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or revolution

indicators.note: blowing top means the word for powder loses its first letter

parts.note: meal is a coarse powder of ground grain

explanation.surface: Someone notices gunpowder blowing the top off during a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powder' suggests gunpowder, but here it is ground grain, meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coming to understand or recognise something for the first time.

clue.text: Contributor to plastics industry prepares individual bottles

indicators.note: bottles means the words prepares individual hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A plastics manufacturer makes individual bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: synthetic gums of this kind are basic raw materials of plastics manufacture.

clue.text: Limit of French horse, tolerating intrusion of cat

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: the horse tolerates the cat coming into it, so the word cat goes inside

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A French horse that only puts up with a cat for so long.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mark out the boundary of something, fixing its limits.

clue.text: Bar selection having no opening for rum

indicators.note: having no removes a letter from the word for selection

parts.note: an excerpt is a selection from a text

indicators.note: opening for takes the first letter of the word rum

explanation.surface: A pub's range lacks any rum to start the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub noun; it is the preposition meaning apart from.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean apart from or other than, as in 'all bar one'.

clue.text: Tea popular in a number of shops

parts.note: cha (or char) is slang for tea
something in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Tea is in vogue across many high-street outlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a business with many branches under one name is a group of linked shops.

clue.text: Write off to armies after a rout

indicators.note: after a rout an army is scattered in disorder, so the letters of to armies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Military losses written off after a crushing defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting sense: to reduce a debt or an asset's value gradually over time, writing it down.

clue.text: One getting up English volume overlooked by student at exam time?

indicators.note: overlooked means the English volume letters are left out of the word for the student

parts.note: a student revising for exams is a reviser

explanation.surface: A student cramming for exams ignores an English textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an early riser is someone getting out of bed.

clue.text: Objections after picking up last of the tab in Newcastle?

definitions.text: last of the tab in Newcastle?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means the word for objections is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Complaints follow someone paying the bar bill in a Geordie pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Newcastle (Geordie) slang a tab is a cigarette, so its last bit is the end left after smoking. 'tab' wants to be a bar bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the butt end of a cigarette, its remaining stump.

clue.text: Vehicle to decline and stop moving — despite such inducements?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to rot is to decay or decline
to stick is to jam and stop moving

explanation.surface: A car that breaks down and stalls however much you coax it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a mix of reward and punishment used to motivate, the donkey's lure and beating.

clue.text: French are bagging new logo, mostly for chamber group?

indicators.note: bagging means the French word holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: es is French for (you) are

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word for logo

parts.note: an emblem is a logo or badge

explanation.surface: French musicians grabbing a fresh logo for their chamber group.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small group of musicians performing chamber music together.

clue.text: I've heard you run round Germany

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A runner circling around Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio procedure word meaning a message has been received and understood.
